newsitem.title: USA: Cambridge Heart delays FDA submission.
newsitem.headline: Cambridge Heart delays FDA submission.

text.p: Cambridge Heart Inc on Wednesday said it delayed its submission to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration regarding labeling claims for its device that measures T-wave alternans.

T-wave alternans are an anomaly detected in heart waves that are measured by an electrocardiogram, Cambridge Heart said. The company is conducting a study to find alternans that are not visible before they lead to sudden cardiac death, it said.

Cambridge Heart already has approval to sell the alternans product for use in stress tests in the United States, but the delay will affect its ability to make claims about the diagnostic and prognostic significance of the results.
The company said the delay, which will hurt revenues n the near to medium term, is caused by a change in the company's study on T-wave alternans and for software updates at its clinical sites.
Cambridge Heart said the delay could last two or three quarters.
The new study design with newer software produced better results than that of the original study design and older software, Cambridge Heart said.
Cambridge Heart said it did not believe the delay involves any basic change or difficulty in the company's underlying science or technology.
